conflicts: Clarity proposes: Consolidate the side panel into a continuous hierarchy: title/context, current turn, a clearly bounded move-history table with readable headers and rows, then controls immediately beneath it. That prioritization is valid only if every requested object, state, and relationship remains visibly substantive; reducing or demoting required content would trade compliance for neatness. Visual System & Craft proposes: Normalize every piece glyph to a consistent optical bounding box, baseline, stroke/shadow treatment, and contrast strategy; make white and black sets equally crisp rather than stylistically asymmetric. System consolidation must not homogenize semantically required elements until their roles become merely decorative. Expressiveness proposes: Develop a distinctive modern-club identity through bespoke piece silhouettes, subtle rank/file ornament, and meaningful turn or last-move emphasis; give the side panel tournament-card details and material indicators that add character without compromising classical legibility. The expressive addition is acceptable only when it strengthens the requested experience rather than replacing required content or interaction evidence.
accept: Accept Clarity's grouping and label-to-object improvements because they make required relationships visibly legible. Accept Craft's cleanup of construction, typography, and state consistency wherever it preserves all required elements. Accept Expressiveness's content-specific imagery and differentiation when it makes the intended game or scene more immediately recognizable.
compromise: Start with the fidelity-critical action: Preserve the exact 8×8 starting position and all 32 pieces, but give white and black pieces unmistakably different fills/outlines while retaining classic glyph silhouettes. Then adopt the other reviewers' hierarchy, token, and expressive refinements within that preserved requirement map. No requested element may be deleted, cropped, reduced to a label, or visually subordinated below its intended role; simplify presentation and unify styling around the complete artifact instead.
